title: Maria Ressa: Understand AI to defend ourselves from ‘predatory’ tech
summary: 'For those who are saying they cannot act: Don’t fall into learned helplessness. When you are the target, you are powerful,' Rappler CEO Maria Ressa says of the fight against artificial intelligence

items: Maria Ressa emphasizes the need to understand artificial intelligence to protect against its predatory nature, which she claims is designed to exploit human biology for profit.
She warns that AI is disrupting attention and agency, contributing to a breakdown in societal complexities and accountability, especially in journalism.
Ressa calls for the establishment of facts and truth to protect democracy and highlights the concentration of AI power among a few companies, urging for better oversight and regulation.

MANILA, Philippines – Understanding artificial intelligence is essential to defending ourselves from the harms of the “predatory, extractive” technology, Rappler chief executive officer and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Ressa said.
During the 2026 Social Good Summit on Saturday, November 21, Ressa warned that AI was built to “hack our biology” as the end goal of Big Tech is profit.
She explained that AI hacked people’s attention, intimacy, and agency, through machine learning in social media, generative chatbots, and agentic AI.

“What have we lost? Sustained attention… our ability to hold complexity, nuances, to move away from identity politics,” Ressa said in her speech, adding that AI is “shifting the evolution of our species.”
“The technology that we’re getting has essentially been predatory and extractive, like mining. How much data have been given, and where has it gone to?”
That defense should be complemented with building own technologies, according to Ressa. (READ: From Duterte to Big Tech: Maria Ressa’s blueprint on fighting back)
This is after Big Tech is “breaking the social contract” by taking and scraping content from news outfits, pushing the journalism industry to already “reaching market failure.”
In 2025, it was found that bots already drove 53% of internet traffic, according to the latest report of cybersecurity firm Imperva.
“For those who are saying they cannot act: Don’t fall into learned helplessness. When you are the target, you are powerful,” she also said.

Ressa also centered on the continued push to protect democracy by establishing facts and truth, in a bid to “reclaiming our future from the machines we built.” (READ: Maria Ressa on AI overreliance: ‘Don’t outsource the nuances’)

“When you don’t have facts and lies spread faster, you cannot actually solve any problem. Not climate change, not rule of law, not child safety. Because if you don’t have facts, you can’t organize. You can’t hold anyone accountable,” she said.
“The chain of facts is what makes a crowd or a mob into ‘we,’ the people. You break that, and there’s no ‘we’ left to reclaim anything.”
Citing the preliminary report of the United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, Ressa said AI is changing geopolitical powers.
Ressa is a co-chair of the 40-member panel, which assesses opportunities, risks, and impacts of AI.

“A few hold the future in their hands, five or six companies, and in terms of compute power, the US has 75% of the world’s compute power. China has 15%, and the EU (European Union), which has put in place the safety measures we need, has 5%,” she said.
She also said that the AI deployment is “far outstripping the ability of law, of audit, and of oversight.”

On Monday, November 16, California sued OpenAI, accusing the company of developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had independently carried out cyberattacks. Among this cyberattacks was the July hack of the open-source platform Hugging Face.
In September, Australia said an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal and gained unauthorized access to files.
“Can we stop impunity in tech?” she asked. – Rappler.com
